proposed_from.topic: Certified exact-risk weighted-random-isolation design for network total effects. For a fixed directed interference graph, its undirected WRI conflict graph C_G, bounded positive integer priority weights, fixed full-neighborhood potential outcomes, and a prespecified finite rule library, write the RDIM error as a 2n-dimensional random linear form and compute each dense risk matrix Q_l exactly. Prove an output-sensitive L n^2 2^{O(w log(w+1))} poly(n,b) algorithm from a width-w tree decomposition by integrating priority-order and reciprocal-count messages, including correctness and bit complexity. Over the graph ellipsoid defined by diag((I+gamma L_C)^{-1},(I+gamma L_C)^{-1}), return the minimax rule mixture, least-favourable endpoint distribution, and primal-dual optimality certificate. For arbitrary graphs give simultaneous operator-norm Monte Carlo regions and a certified worst-case-risk gap. Consumer: a universal-financial-education versus none follow-up to Cai, de Janvry, and Sadoulet's rural-China insurance diffusion experiment. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Every RDIM risk entry was reduced to one- and two-marked isolated-set count probabilities, including odd counts and bias. Integer-weight risks have polynomial output bit length, and a three-state polynomial recurrence was derived and checked by exact enumeration on three forests and 344 matrix entries. Two bidirected three-leaf stars force isolated-set size two; reciprocal hub/leaf rules produce distinct verified risks. Checks covered local-max versus sequential greedy semantics, directed-star legality, parity denominators, rationality, PSD ellipsoid, generic SDP reduction, treewidth hardness, and recent design papers. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Compress joined separator priority/count messages to 2^{O(w log(w+1))} poly(n,b) size; the direct construction retains (nb)^{O(w)} coefficients and proves only XP complexity. EARLY KILL TEST: On all width-two/three graphs with n≤9 and weights in {1,2,3}, compare every tagged coefficient with exhaustive priority ordering, then derive the symbolic message-size recurrence; any unavoidable (nb)^w factor or parameter-preserving hardness obstruction kills the promised FPT kernel and forces pivot. seed_details.title: Exact marked-risk oracle: fixed-parameter compression or hardness
seed_details.anchor_location: Algorithm 3, Theorem 4.1, Appendix S2.1, and Section 6
seed_details.opened_evidence: Algorithm 3 defines the sequential weighted isolation law; Theorem 4.1 bounds RDIM risk by representativeness and reciprocal isolated-arm sizes; Appendix S2.1 supplies the surrogate proof; Section 6 identifies rigorous theory and computationally effective probability approximation as open.
seed_details.proof_boundary: Replace the surrogate by the exact dense quadratic risk and decide whether all one- and two-marked reciprocal-count moments admit an output-sensitive \(2^{O(w\log(w+1))}\operatorname{poly}(n,b)\) oracle or are parameterized-hard.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: At a tree-decomposition join, synchronize relative bag priorities, selected-versus-blocked labels, and the isolated-count generating variable without expanding \((nb)^{O(w)}\) monomials.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for the exact target--method pair using random greedy maximal independent sets, marked moments, reciprocal counts, and treewidth found asymptotic occupancy results and an \(\widetilde O(n^{w+3})\) linear-extension analogue, but no WRI marked-risk oracle.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from ordinary bounded-treewidth dynamic programming because maximal independent sets are monadic-second-order definable.
seed_details.rebuttal: The design probability is a weighted measure over priority orders, not a count of independent sets; Eiben et al. show that order counting can remain non-FPT at bounded cover-graph treewidth, and the direct WRI polynomial messages have \((nb)^{O(w)}\) size.
seed_details.burned_reason: The separator-compression angle ended with only a forest oracle and an XP diagnostic; the proposed hardness retry restated the open branch without a source problem, gadget, coefficient identity, or treewidth map.

seed_details.title: Parameterized hardness of a single marked WRI moment
seed_details.anchor_location: Theorem 1 and Section 3, especially the equitable-coloring reduction and flower gadgets; Section 5
seed_details.opened_evidence: Theorem 1 rules out an FPT algorithm for counting linear extensions parameterized by cover-graph treewidth unless \(\mathrm{W[1]}=\mathrm{FPT}\); the proof encodes equitable coloring through congruences while controlling treewidth; the conclusion leaves finer counting classifications open.
seed_details.proof_boundary: Encode the order constraints of the source problem into the probability that one or two marked vertices survive sequential WRI while preserving the conflict-graph treewidth.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The poset flower gadget must be replaced by a domination gadget whose weighted priority-order probability is recoverable from a tagged isolated-set coefficient.
seed_details.destination_search: No parameter-preserving reduction to weighted random greedy isolation was located; the closest positive analogue is Kangas, Koivisto, and Salonen's XP tree-decomposition algorithm.
seed_details.red_team: Eiben et al.'s hardness already settles this because WRI also integrates priority orders.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their oracle counts linear extensions of a poset, while WRI accepts orders through a graph domination certificate; neither a parsimonious nor a Turing reduction preserving treewidth is available.
seed_details.disposition: dropped-after-ranking because the positive-or-negative dichotomy subsumes it

seed_details.title: Marked-moment characterization of exact RDIM risk
seed_details.opened_evidence: The paper targets the finite-population total effect and selects WRI weights by a degree-distribution and inverse-size surrogate rather than by the exact bias-plus-variance matrix.
seed_details.proof_boundary: Express RDIM error as a \(2n\)-coordinate random linear form and recover every risk entry from isolated-set count polynomials tagged by at most two vertices, retaining odd counts and random denominators.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the Lipschitz surrogate inequality in the proof of Theorem 4.1 by conditional hypergeometric products and an exact expansion of \(\mathbb E[(e-d)(e-d)^{\mathsf T}]\).
seed_details.destination_search: Exact-title and formula searches found no paper deriving the full dense RDIM risk matrix for WRI.
seed_details.red_team: This is only a routine covariance expansion of the estimator in Shi et al.
seed_details.rebuttal: The expansion is a necessary but insufficient contribution; it survives only as the reduction that defines the nontrivial marked counting oracle.
seed_details.disposition: dropped as a standalone seed and retained as Proposition 1

seed_details.title: Least-favourable spectral certificate for a finite WRI library
seed_details.opened_evidence: AWRI simulates a surrogate over candidate weights and selects one rule; it does not randomize across the library against exact ellipsoidal RDIM risk.
seed_details.proof_boundary: Convert exact rule risks into an eigenvalue minimax game and derive a primal--dual certificate valid with zero mixture weights and repeated leading eigenspaces.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace scalar surrogate minimization by the epigraph constraint \(\sum_{\ell}q_{\ell}Q_{\ell}\preceq tH^{-1}\) and interpret the dual PSD matrix as a finite distribution over ellipsoid endpoints.
seed_details.destination_search: Duarte, Sagnol, and Wong provide semidefinite minimax-design machinery, and Viviano et al. optimize cluster partitions, but neither result supplies exact WRI risks or the stated endpoint certificate.
seed_details.red_team: The minimax mixture is an immediate E-optimal design SDP.
seed_details.rebuttal: The SDP is standard once the risk matrices exist, so this seed is not tier-bearing and is retained only as a certified design consequence of the exact oracle.
seed_details.disposition: dropped as a standalone seed and retained as Theorem 6

seed_details.title: Simultaneous operator-norm risk regions on arbitrary graphs
seed_details.anchor_location: Section 4.1.3, the exact-probability hardness result, Monte Carlo probability construction, and Section 7
seed_details.opened_evidence: Randomized graph clustering makes design-law quantities accessible through offline resampling even when exact exposure probabilities are hard, but its guarantees concern exposure probabilities and estimator variance rather than dense RDIM risk selection.
seed_details.proof_boundary: Construct independent self-adjoint per-draw risk contributions and propagate simultaneous matrix Bernstein regions through the mixture eigenvalue game.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Estimate \(aa^{\mathsf T}\) directly, rather than separately estimating marginal exposure probabilities, so random reciprocal counts and bias remain inside each draw.
seed_details.destination_search: Tropp's Theorem 1.4 supplies the matrix concentration step; no located network-design paper propagates simultaneous rule-matrix regions into a certified post-selection minimax gap.
seed_details.red_team: This follows immediately from matrix Bernstein and Weyl's inequality.
seed_details.rebuttal: That objection holds for the generic concentration branch, so it is retained only as an arbitrary-graph fallback and not as the proposal kernel.
seed_details.disposition: dropped as a standalone seed and retained as Theorem 7

seed_details.title: Studentized design-based RDIM limit after graph-only rule mixing
seed_details.opened_evidence: The consistency discussion is simulation-based and the conclusion explicitly requests more rigorous finite-population theory; no studentized RDIM limit law is supplied.
seed_details.proof_boundary: Derive uniform stabilization of the random isolated-set denominators and a conditional-to-unconditional CLT over a finite graph-only rule library.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Unlike a fixed exposure-indicator dependency graph, WRI first generates a random greedy support whose membership can depend on distant priority changes; the proof must localize or martingale-decompose this support before studentization.
seed_details.destination_search: Gao and Ding and Kandiros et al. provide design-based covariance and coverage for different exposure estimators; Chin provides dependency-graph Stein bounds; none treats RDIM's random greedy support and reciprocal denominators.
seed_details.red_team: Condition on the isolated set and apply the complete-randomization central limit theorem.
seed_details.rebuttal: Unconditioning adds random support, representativeness bias, and unstable reciprocal denominators; uniform control over graph-only rule selection is not supplied by a conditional theorem.

seed_details.title: Robust WRI risk over plausible interference graphs
seed_details.anchor_location: Setup assumption that the network is fixed and known, and Section 6 discussion of noisy or unobserved networks
seed_details.opened_evidence: The design is conditional on one known directed graph, while the conclusion identifies weighted, noisy, and unobserved social networks as a substantive limitation.
seed_details.proof_boundary: Optimize WRI risk over a compactly represented family of graph completions without enumerating all edge augmentations.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Graph-specific isolation must become a joint state over selected vertices and unresolved candidate edges because every completion changes the conflict graph and its risk law.
seed_details.destination_search: The closest robust-network papers average or bound across plausible networks but do not compute exact finite-population WRI risk; no compact separation oracle for this design class was located.
seed_details.red_team: Take the maximum of the fixed-graph risk matrices already computed for each candidate graph.
seed_details.rebuttal: That requires enumerating exponentially many completions and does not address the joint isolation-law change; the current substrate does not yet yield a credible compact oracle.

seed_details.title: Necessary-and-sufficient finite-library minimax frontier
seed_details.anchor_location: Proposition 2.2, Appendix A.5, and Section 6 conjectures
seed_details.opened_evidence: Proposition 2.2 identifies unrestricted network-experiment minimax risk with a function of the exposure conflict graph through distributions over maximal independent sets, while leaving the function implicit; the computational section conjectures severe approximation hardness.
seed_details.proof_boundary: Characterize exactly when the convex hull of a prespecified WRI library's dense RDIM risk matrices reaches the unrestricted random-isolation benchmark.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace optimization over all maximal-independent-set laws and all estimators by a dual separation condition for the library risk hull, while retaining the RDIM restriction on one side.
seed_details.destination_search: Finite optimal-design equivalence theorems and conflict-graph minimax theory provide adjacent convex duality, but no result identifies equality between a WRI-rule hull with RDIM and the unrestricted isolation benchmark.
seed_details.red_team: Equality is just membership of the unrestricted optimizer in the convex hull of library rules.
seed_details.rebuttal: The unrestricted comparator jointly varies designs and estimators and is only implicitly characterized; a graph-computable necessary-and-sufficient condition would require a new separation or orbit-compression theorem.
